answer.rationale: Two hours ago a release went out and now p99 write-path latency is climbing 5x in the primary region, with settlement traffic at peak. The inherited record on rolling back (b1) says a rollback cleared a checkout error spike, the prior build was stable, and the rollback finished without customer impact. That is the strongest directly applicable precedent for this exact signal pattern (release-correlated write-path degradation). Staged-gating memory (b6) shows bad builds have been caught and rolled back before; provisioning memory (b3) speaks to capacity, not releases. Choosing rollback as the single intervention matches the primary objective: a failed-fast, contained recovery that preserves customer writes. The 1-memory verification budget is spent on b1 to confirm the rollback procedure is genuinely safe under settlement-peak conditions before committing. Capacity and circuit-breaker options are held for the next window in case rollback does not resolve the climb.
